title: TikTok, DOT launch interactive virtual heritage site tours
summary: The Department of Tourism has tapped social media platform TikTok to promote UNESCO-recognized heritage sites in the country through immersive livestreaming tours.

blocks.text: The program, which features content creators Jeane Pauline and Reb Atadero touring San Agustin Church and Museum in Intramuros, Manila, is the first edition of its kind in Southeast Asia.
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Tourism has tapped social media platform TikTok to promote UNESCO-recognized heritage sites in the country through immersive livestreaming tours.
The live tour generated nearly six million impressions, with 73,000 viewers from Southeast Asia, the United Kingdom and Australia, according to TikTok.
The program also features real-time conversations, allowing viewers to interact with the virtual tour by asking questions.

“TikTok is a really good platform for us to start talking and start learning about heritage. Content creators have the ability to start these conversations. It doesn’t have to be too academic or technical,” said Ivan Anthony Henares, secretary-general of the UNESCO National Commission of the Philippines.

“Beyond entertainment, we want to see more content creators use their talents to bring heritage to life, share their personal stories and create educational content that inspires meaningful engagement,” said Chin Zhao Wei, TikTok LIVE brand and reputation manager.
The collaboration aims to create more opportunities for cultural institutions, experts and creators to share Philippine heritage with wider audiences through responsible storytelling.
